topic.title: AI made the documents longer
topic.claim: AI was meant to make work faster; in most offices it made documents three times longer and decisions no quicker.
topic.moment: A meeting summary with six headings and a 'key takeaways' box nobody scrolls to.

turn.believed: AI at work is making people more productive.
turn.actually: It mostly makes people look thorough, so everyone produces more pages for others to skim.

topic.because: Length still looks like effort to a busy boss. When writing costs nothing, the reader pays the cost instead.
topic.payoff: Before you send the AI version, ask if you'd have written half of it by hand. If not, delete that half.
topic.behaviour: People paste AI-written notes, decks and emails that are longer than needed; colleagues feed them back into AI to summarise.
topic.mechanism: Effort is judged by volume, and AI makes volume free.
topic.group: Desk workers using AI tools daily
topic.send_to: The colleague whose emails got four bullet points longer this year.
topic.why_now: Most offices now have AI tools switched on by default, and the side effects are visible in every inbox.

score.why: Matches his belief that AI at work is used to look busy; the six-heading summary nobody reads is instantly familiar.
